item.title: March 4, 2026: CCO Ithaca – Boulangerie
item.description: The Cayuga Chamber Orchestra presents “Boulangerie” on Saturday evening, celebrating the impact of Nadia Boulanger. Guillaume Pirard, Music Director, and Sarah Chandler, Executive Director, joined host Diane Jones to chat about the achievements of her students, including Aaron Copland and Thea Musgrave. We also spoke about CCO Principal Horn Steven Harmon stepping to the front of the stage for Mozart’s Horn Concerto No. 4. More about the Cayuga Chamber Orchestra is available here.

item.title: March 5, 2026: SO – Meet Jacob Joyce
item.description: Time to meet another Music Director candidate for the Syracuse Orchestra. We spoke to Jacob Joyce about the concert, the excitement of working with the orchestra, and his philosophy of the role of the orchestra in the community. More about the Syracuse Orchestra is available here. And learn about Jacob Joyce at his website.

item.title: “The D.O.T. P.O.D.”: Hobbies
item.description: When you think of the New York State Department of Transportation, you probably imagine projects, planning, or filling potholes and snowplowing. And while that’s definitely part of the job, DOT employees don’t just live and breathe transportation. They’ve got plenty of hobbies and passions outside of work. item.title: Science Today with Dr. Rich Kopecky – Episode 45
item.description: Do animals experience joy? Most people think they do, but proving it is a different story. Learn about scientific efforts to measure animal happiness. Also this month on Science Today, find out about “pre-rehab” which may improve surgical outcomes, and how a plant can survive exposure to outer space.

item.title: CNY Heroes, Episode 41 – Assemblyman Bill Magnarelli Discusses the annual CNY Veterans Parade
item.description: On this edition of CNY Heroes, Dan’s guest is Syracuse State Assemblyman Bill Magnarelli. In 2008, he was the driving force behind re-establishing the annual CNY Veterans Parade and Expo at the NYS Fairgrounds. The early November event features dozens of veteran and military groups and draws thousands of spectators. item.title: Repeating History, Episode 18 – Dr. Angela Murphy, Professor of History at Texas State University
item.description: On the latest episode of Repeating History, we welcome Dr. Angela Murphy, Professor of History at Texas State University. Our topic today is the extraordinary life of Syracuse’s own “defiant fugitive” Rev. Jermain W. Loguen, the Underground Railroad King and tireless freedom fighter. item.title: Our New Neighbors, Episode 32 – Nina Polukhina
item.description: On this edition of Our New Neighbors, host Maryna Bagovska is joined by Nina Polukhina a Russian immigrant who moved to America after marrying her childhood friend. Several years later Nina is now a mother of three children with a passion for photography. In this discussion Nina discusses the challenges she faced as an immigrant as well as offering advice for those in similar circumstances.
